story.titleZh: F1新马德里赛道为何被称为“赛车杀手”
story.summaryZh: 本周末马德里大奖赛将启用全新马德里赛道赛道，该赛道被比作摩纳哥、澳门和吉达的结合体，但F3测试中出现的19次红旗和多辆赛车损坏引发对其“赛车杀手”特性的担忧。
story.originalTitle: Why F1's new Madrid track is a 'car killer'
story.summaryEn: This weekend's Madrid Grand Prix will debut the brand-new Madring circuit, which has been compared to a mix of Monaco, Macau and Jeddah, but fears about its "car killer" nature have arisen after 19 red flags and multiple damaged cars in an F3 test.
detailZh: 一级方程式的新西班牙大奖赛场地被形容为“赛车杀手”。
全新的马德里赛道赛道将于本周末举办史上第一场比赛，但直到现在F1车手们才开始意识到这条赛道将带来多么巨大的挑战。
已经驾驶过这条赛道的人将其描述为摩纳哥、澳门和吉达的混合体。
这是一条老派赛道，拥有真正的特色和有可能成为经典瞬间的弯角。但也有人担心它会带来什么样的比赛，以及对赛车和车手会有多么残酷。
在6月赛道建设期间探索过该赛道后，我们进一步深入研究了这条赛道究竟会带来什么样的挑战，以及本周末我们可以期待什么。
最大的指示是几周前在那里举行的为期两天的F3测试。
“在F3测试中出现了19次红旗和三个损坏的底盘、损坏的悬挂……好吧，他们是F3车手，但这是一条杀死赛车的赛道，”威廉姆斯F1车队领队James Vowles告诉西班牙媒体Sport。
The 比赛了解到，一些F3车队对不得不在那里测试感到不太满意，因为损坏零件清单非常长。
但那次F3测试作为F1马德里赛事的试播集非常有价值，这是赛道组织者要求的，试图避免拉斯维加斯首秀时出现的那些问题——当时失控的排水盖干扰了练习赛，撞毁了塞恩斯的法拉利，并激怒了车队领队Fred Vasseur。
混乱的F3测试也为F1车队和车手敲响了警钟，让他们意识到这将是一个多么大的挑战。
法拉利曾在7月在那里进行了一次F1拍摄日，但那时赛道版本要粗糙得多，所以F3的测试才是该场地的第一次正式测试。
让F1车队和车手担忧的是，F3中的19次红旗分散在赛道各处（见下文）。这意味着不仅仅有一个危险区域需要应对，而是有很多地方你可能出错并面临巨额维修账单。
由于许多车队要在2026年成本上限内计算剩余的开发预算，他们最不希望的就是赛车被撞毁。
我们采访了几位F3车手和车队，以了解为什么马德里赛道在这么多不同方面都如此具有挑战性，以及为什么会有这么多红旗。
当被问及为什么它如此具有挑战性时，奥迪支持的F3锦标赛领先者Freddie Slater告诉The 比赛：“因为那里的弯角非常紧，不容犯错，而且出弯时墙壁会向你逼近。它们不像大多数赛道那样远离你。”
“你总是出弯时试图远离它，而不是最大化利用，所以这是一条很难找到节奏的赛道。”
“你必须推进，否则你就慢。所以我认为这就是为什么它会造成这么多撞车，因为如果你不推进，你就没有达到极限。”
“但老实说，在我看来它可能是赛历上最好的赛道之一，因为它有那种老派的感觉。有点像一些老派的英国赛道、澳门之类的地方。所以我真的很兴奋能在那里举行[F3锦标赛]决赛。”
马德里赛道的一圈从类似吉达的低速减速弯开始，然后是3号和4号弯的全速冲刺，接着进入第一个真正的危险区域——第二个减速弯。
这是一个高速减速弯，出弯时墙壁肯定会向你逼近，也是测试中许多F3赛车被撞毁的地方。
“那里有很多圈速可赚，因为之后是上坡路段，所以上坡时有很多圈速可以争取，”Slater说。
“这就是为什么我看到很多人为了最大圈速而冒险，但这也可能是撞车最多的地方。”
“此外，路肩也不太宽容，所以你必须做对，否则就会撞车。”
这本质上是现已移除的新加坡Sling三顶点弯的更困难版本，轨迹是“如果稍微出错就会头朝墙壁撞去”。它不像虚拟世界中的一些圈那样看起来可以轻松跳过路肩。
而且减速弯的入口是赛道上仅有的两个直线模式区域之一，所以车手们将以约340公里/小时（211英里/小时）的速度到达。这绝对不是你想要出现直线模式故障的地方，就像今年早些时候维斯塔潘的红牛那样。
通过那个墙壁后，你驶入地下通道下方，开始上坡，通过另一个棘手的路段，那里也让许多F3赛车成为受害者。
赛道的突出特征是倾斜的La Monumental弯，但实际上在它之前的弯角在测试中让同样多的F3车手吃亏。
有一个紧凑的减速弯，接着是10号和11号弯的快速右/左连续弯，非常容易出错。
然后你将进入La Monumental，一个24%的倾斜弯，其挑战性使赞德沃特的倾斜弯相形见绌。
倍耐力的首席工程师Simone Berra将其称为锦标赛中“最严酷的弯角”，当The 比赛问他与赞德沃特的倾斜弯相比如何时，Berra说La Monumental对轮胎施加的能量高出20%到30%。
此外，它的出口完全盲区，而且是抓地力限制而非像赞德沃特倾斜弯那样的动力限制，也就是说，为了给车手所需的抓地力，对轮胎和赛车造成了巨大压力。
F3车手在测试中尝试了许多不同的线路，预计F1车手在周五也会这样做。
“感觉就像我在开印地赛车[在椭圆赛道上]，”Slater告诉The 比赛。
“所以是的，这很酷。在F3赛车中它几乎就是全油门。我认为在F2甚至F1中会稍微困难一些。”
“但很难找到正确的线路，因为显然在坡顶处，托底可能会很严重。看起来是一个容易的弯角，但实际上驾驶它，要找到节奏是相当困难的。”
La Monumental只是单圈的一半，之后还有更多具有挑战性的弯角，比如紧凑的17号右弯。
整圈几乎没有喘息的空间，保守驾驶也行不通。
蒙扎F3冲刺赛冠军加藤大翔解释说：“如果你想获得圈速，你必须推进到接近墙壁，所以这很冒险但驾驶起来很有趣。”
F1车手们在蒙扎的车手巡游中交换了对马德里的第一印象，Sainz透露“每个人似乎都对马德里推出的赛道感到相当震惊”。
Sainz，作为本大奖赛的大使，解释说他的意思是震惊于F1增加了一条真正有特色的赛道，而不是近年来加入赛历的一些较为平淡的街道赛道。
detailEn: Formula 1’s new Spanish Grand Prix venue has been described as a “car killer”.
The first-ever race at the brand-new Madring circuit will take place this weekend, but only now are F1 drivers starting to realise what a huge challenge the circuit is going to be.
It’s been described as a mix of Monaco, Macau and Jeddah by those who have already driven it.

It’s an old-school circuit with proper character and corners that have the potential to be instant classics. But there are fears about what kind of race it will produce and how brutal it could be for the cars and drivers.
Having explored the circuit during its construction in June, we’ve since dug more into exactly what kind of challenge the track will present and what we can expect this weekend.
The biggest indicator of that was the two-day Formula 3 test held there a couple of weeks ago.

“In the Formula 3 test there were 19 red flags and three broken chassis, broken suspensions…OK, they’re Formula 3 drivers, but it’s a track that kills cars,” Williams F1 team principal James Vowles told Spanish outlet Sport.
The Race understands some F3 teams were less than impressed by having to test there, because the damaged parts list was very long.

But that F3 test was highly valuable as a pilot episode for F1’s Madrid event, one requested by the circuit organiser to try to avoid the kind of issues that plagued Las Vegas’s debut when errant drain covers disrupted practice, wrecked Carlos Sainz’s Ferrari and infuriated team principal Fred Vasseur.
The chaotic F3 test has also acted as a warning sign for F1 teams and drivers about how much of a challenge it will be.
Ferrari conducted an F1 filming day there back in July, but that was on a much rougher version of the circuit, so the F3 running was the first proper test for the venue.

What’s worrying F1 teams and drivers is that the 19 red flags in F3 were scattered throughout the circuit (see below). It means there isn’t just one danger zone to navigate, as there are so many places where you can come unstuck and find yourself with a hefty repair bill.
With many teams working out their remaining development budget within the 2026 cost cap, the last thing they’ll want is a wrecked car.
We spoke to several F3 drivers and teams to find out why the Madring is so challenging in so many different ways and why there were so many red flags.

Asked why it’s so challenging, Audi-backed F3 championship leader Freddie Slater told The Race: “Because the corners that are there, they're so tight and they're not forgiving and also the walls come at you on the exit of the corners. They don't go away from you like most tracks.
“You're always coming out of the corner and trying to drive away from it instead of maximising, so it's a very tricky track to get in the rhythm of things.
“You have to push otherwise you're slow. So I think that's why it creates so many crashes because if you don't push you're just not on the limit.

“But honestly it's probably one of the best tracks on the calendar in my opinion, just because it's got that old-school feeling to it. Kind of like some of the old-school UK tracks, Macau, places like that. So I'm really excited to have the [F3 championship] finale there.”
The Madring lap starts with a slow-speed chicane akin to Jeddah’s, followed by a flat-out blast through Turns 3 and 4, which builds up into the first real danger zone - the second chicane.
It’s a high-speed chicane where the wall certainly comes at you on the exit, and it was the site of many a crumpled F3 car in the test.
“That's where there's so much laptime because there's uphill section after that, so there's so much laptime to gain going uphill,” Slater said.
“That's why I see a lot of people risking obviously for maximum laptime but also it's probably the place where the most crashes are.
“Also the kerbs are not very forgiving so you have to get it correct otherwise, you're going to end up crashing.”

It’s essentially an even harder version of the now-removed triple-apex Singapore Sling where the trajectory is 'head-first into the wall if you get it slightly wrong'. It’s not anything like some of the laps in the virtual world make it look where you’re able to effortlessly skip over the kerbs.

And the entry to the chicane is one of only two straight mode zones on the circuit, so drivers will be arriving at around 340km/h (211mph). It’s certainly not the kind of place you’d want a straight mode failure like those on Max Verstappen’s Red Bull earlier this year.
Negotiate that wall and you drive beneath the underpass and start climbing uphill through another tricky session that also claimed many an F3 car as a victim.
The standout feature of the circuit is the banked La Monumental corner but actually the corners just before it caught out just as many F3 drivers in the test.
There’s a tight chicane followed by a quick right/left in quick succession at Turns 10 and 11 that’s very easy to get wrong.
That then propels you into La Monumental, a 24% banked corner that dwarfs the challenge of Zandvoort’s banked turns.

Pirelli’s chief engineer Simone Berra labelled it “the most severe turn” in the championship and when The Race asked him how it compared to Zandvoort’s banking, Berra said La Monumental places 20 to 30% higher energy on the tyres.

Plus it has a completely blind exit and it’s grip-limited rather than power-limited like Zandvoort’s banked corner is, i.e. it’s a huge strain on the tyres and cars to give the drivers the grip they need.
F3 drivers were trying lots of different lines during the test and expect F1 drivers to do the same on Friday.
"It feels like I'm in an IndyCar [on an oval]," Slater told The Race.
"So yeah, it's pretty cool. It's just about flat, probably, in a Formula 3 car. I think it's going to be a little bit more difficult in your Formula 2 and maybe even Formula 1.

"But it's quite difficult to get the right line because obviously where the crest is, the bottoming can get quite bad. It looks an easy corner when you look at it but actually to drive it, it's quite a difficult corner to get the rhythm."
La Monumental only marks the halfway point in the lap and there are plenty more challenging corners after that, like the tight Turn 17 right-hander.
There’s very little breathing room around the lap and going conservative doesn’t work either.
Monza F3 sprint race winner Taito Kato explained: “If you want to gain laptime, you have to push until you’re close to the wall, so it’s risky but fun to drive.”
F1 drivers were swapping first impressions of Madrid on the drivers’ parade at Monza, with Sainz revealing “everyone seemed quite shocked by the track that Madrid has come up with”.

Sainz, who is an ambassador for this grand prix, explained he meant shocked in terms of F1 adding a track that has actual character, as opposed to some of the blander street tracks that have joined the calendar in recent years.

赛道包含多个危险区域，包括高速弯、颠簸的弯道和24%倾斜的La Monumental弯，对轮胎和赛车造成巨大压力。
F3车手Freddie Slater和Taito Kato描述了赛道的挑战性，强调需要冒险推进才能获得圈速，但容易导致撞车。
keyPointsEn: Williams team principal James Vowles said the F3 test saw 19 red flags, three broken chassis and broken suspensions, calling it a "track that kills cars."
The circuit features multiple danger zones, including high-speed chicanes, bumpy corners and the 24% banked La Monumental corner, placing huge strain on tyres and cars.
F3 drivers Freddie Slater and Taito Kato described the track's challenges, emphasizing the need to push to the limit for lap time, which easily leads to crashes.

detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔夺得杆位，梅赛德斯车队在卡塔尔大奖赛排位赛中占据领先，这是自5月份加拿大大奖赛以来的首次。

relatedItems.titleZh: 安东内利与梅赛德斯包揽卡塔尔大奖赛练习赛
relatedItems.summaryZh: 基米·安东内利在卡塔尔大奖赛FP3练习赛中连续三次夺冠，梅赛德斯竞争对手似乎在争夺最佳非梅赛德斯车队，红牛在第三次练习赛中取得第三名。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Antonelli and Mercedes sweep Qatar GP practice
detailZh: 基米·安东内利在卡塔尔大奖赛FP3练习赛中连续三次夺冠，梅赛德斯竞争对手似乎在争夺最佳非梅赛德斯车队，红牛在第三次练习赛中取得第三名。
在排位赛前的20分钟内，练习赛中的圈数非常少。似乎很少有车手能在他们的第一次排位赛中取得更好的成绩。
安东内利的队友乔治·拉塞尔在第二阶段的表现中保持了领先，尽管他在著名的14号弯角发生了一次打滑，那里的地板损坏总是令人担忧，这使安东内利得以缩小到落后0.017秒。
但在第三次尝试中，安东内利全速前进，逆转了排名，领先拉塞尔0.249秒，这个成绩无人能及。
梅赛德斯的车手在任何时刻都落后了半秒左右，红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘在练习结束时排名第三，落后安东内利0.510秒。
维斯塔潘的队友伊萨克·哈德贾排名第四，领先略有提升的法拉利车手查尔斯·勒克莱尔，勒克莱尔在周五的比赛中表现不佳，非常悲观。
勒克莱尔的队友刘易斯·汉密尔顿排名第九，抱怨赛车转向不足，并要求增加前翼角度以避免提前进站。
奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂在最后一次性能测试跑之前排名第三，但在第六和第七位时被麦凯轮车队的兰多·诺里斯超越，最终排名下降。
皮亚斯特里是众多抱怨转向不足的车手之一。
小红牛在周五表现得非常乐观，并在FP3练习中领跑中游，Arvid Lindblad排名第八，劳森排名第十，领先其中游对手两十分。
阿尔派恩落后小红牛很多，小红牛在车队积分榜上领先Enstone车队27分，争夺第五名。加斯利在FP3练习中排名第14，队友科拉平托排名第16。
科拉平托在最后阶段幸运地避开了高速移动的斯特罗尔，这一事件将在练习结束后进行调查。
在劳森和加斯利之间是奥迪和哈斯车队的奥利·贝尔曼，他的队友拉斐尔·卡马拉排名第15。
费尔南多·阿隆索超越了两辆威廉姆斯赛车，为阿斯顿·马丁赢得了第17名。
凯迪拉克车队以瓦尔特里·博塔斯领先近0.7秒的成绩，排在最后一名塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯之前。
第17名 费尔南多·阿隆索（阿斯顿·马丁）+2.696秒
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli completed a hat-trick of practice sweeps in FP3 for the Qatar Grand Prix, as Mercedes' rivals appear to be fighting for the best of the rest with Red Bull taking that honour in third practice.
Very few laps were turned in the first 20 minutes or so, before qualifying runs. It appeared that few drivers could improve on their first qualifying efforts.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell set the early pace and maintained that lead after the second performance runs despite a wide moment through the notorious Turn 14 - where floor damage is always a worry - and that allowed Antonelli to close in to just 0.017s behind.
But on the third attempts, Antonelli turned on the afterburners to flip the order and lead Russell by 0.249s, which would not be beaten.
Mercedes' challengers were regularly around half a second down at any given point, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen taking third at the end of the session, 0.510s adrift of Antonelli.
Verstappen's team-mate Isack Hadjar took fourth ahead of the slightly improved Ferrari of Charles Leclerc, who was very pessimistic after Friday's running.
Leclerc's team-mate Lewis Hamilton was down in ninth, complaining that the car was not turning in sufficiently and asking for more front wing angle to avoid understeer.
Oscar Piastri had been third before the last performance run attempt, but was jumped by McLaren team-mate Lando Norris as they ran sixth and seventh, shuffled down the order by the end.
Piastri was another of the many drivers complaining of understeer.
Racing Bulls was extremely bullish on Friday and did head the midfield in FP3 with Arvid Lindblad in eighth and Liam Lawson in 10th, two tenths clear of its midfield rivals.

Alpine was well behind Racing Bulls, which is 27 points ahead of the Enstone team in the chase for fifth in the constructors' standings. Pierre Gasly finished 14th and team-mate Franco Colapinto 16th in FP3.
Colapinto was lucky to avoid a slow-moving Lance Stroll at high speed in the closing stages and that incident will be investigated after the session.
Between Lawson and Gasly were the Audis and Haas driver Ollie Bearman, whose team-mate Rafael Camara finished 15th.
Fernando Alonso cleared both Williams to take 17th for Aston Martin.
Cadillac anchored the order with Valtteri Bottas nearly 0.7s ahead of last-place Sergio Perez.
17 Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) +2.696s
keyPointsZh: 梅赛德斯竞争对手在练习赛中落后梅赛德斯约半秒。
keyPointsEn: Mercedes' challengers were around half a second behind at any given point.

relatedItems.titleZh: 韩泰启动F1轮胎测试并接触车队，准备竞标2029年供应合同
relatedItems.summaryZh: 韩泰已启动F1轮胎测试计划并与车队展开谈判，准备竞标从2029年起成为F1官方轮胎供应商。F1当前与倍耐力的合同持续到2028年底。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Hankook emerges with serious F1 tyre supply push
relatedItems.summaryEn: Hankook has begun a Formula 1 tyre testing programme and opened talks with teams as it prepares to bid to become the official F1 tyre supplier from 2029. F1's current contract with Pirelli runs until the end of 2028.
detailZh: 据The Race了解，韩泰已启动一项F1轮胎测试计划，并与车队展开谈判，为竞标从2029年起成为大奖赛官方供应商做准备。
F1目前与倍耐力的合同持续到2028年底。此前，这家意大利公司击败普利司通的竞争性报价，赢得了F1最近一次招标合同，覆盖2025至2027年。
今年6月，在国际汽联行使选择权后，其合同又延长了一个赛季。
然而，从2029年起，国际汽联将启动新的招标程序，届时似乎将出现新的竞争，以争夺F1官方供应商资格。
据了解，倍耐力希望先等待看到招标细节，然后再决定是否参与竞标，以延长其自2011年以来的当前合约期，而普利司通长期以来一直在评估重返F1的可能性，其代表已出席过多场比赛。
然而，现在有消息显示，韩泰也准备加入竞争，并且一直在暗中加大自身的努力。
该公司的代表被发现出现在最近的拉斯维加斯大奖赛上，据了解，这是他们继9月前往马德里之后，今年第二次造访F1比赛。
据The Race了解，韩泰利用这些行程会见了大多数车队，并与老板、首席执行官和其他高级管理人员讨论了计划。
然而，前往各地观看比赛——其中还包括2025年在中国、日本和新加坡举行的赛事——只是其为2029年做准备的努力的一方面。
据了解，韩泰已在公司内部组建了一支44人的专项工作组，为进入F1做准备。
除了投入研发能力和模拟器运行之外，该公司今年还使用一辆改装的F2同级测试车完成了两次F1轮胎开发测试，以评估潜在的轮胎结构以及不同配方。
第三次测试已安排用于研发其雨地轮胎，该公司希望这也能帮助其开发出一款具有更窄水雾羽流的轮胎，以减少湿地条件下造成的能见度问题。
韩泰也在努力进行生产和制造规划，以满足任何轮胎招标合同下供应F1、F2和F3轮胎所需。
韩泰对国际汽联的赛事当然并不陌生，这家韩国公司已经是世界拉力锦标赛的官方轮胎供应商，并且刚刚结束了对电动方程式锦标赛的供应，而普利司通将在即将到来的赛季接替。今年早些时候，韩泰还被指定为该管理机构的全球合作伙伴。
2029年之后的新F1轮胎招标期几乎肯定会涵盖向下一个规则时代的过渡，F1正着眼于更轻、更灵活的新赛车，以配合从2030年开始改用V8动力单元。
这些计划还将包括一种新的轮胎设计，该设计将比目前的18英寸设计略微减小车轮尺寸。
detailEn: Hankook has begun a Formula 1 tyre testing programme and opened talks with teams as it prepares to bid on becoming grand prix racing’s official supplier from 2029, The Race has learned.

F1’s current contract with Pirelli runs until the end of 2028, after the Italian company won F1’s most recent tender deal, which covered the period from 2025-2027, against a rival bid from Bridgestone.
Its contract was extended by a further season in June this year after an option was taken up by the FIA.
From 2029, however, a new tender process is set to be launched by the FIA and there looks set to be fresh competition to secure the right to be the official F1 supplier.

It is understood that Pirelli wants to wait to see details of the tender before deciding if it enters the fray to extend its current spell which stretches back to 2011, while Bridgestone has long evaluated an F1 return with representatives having attended races.
However, it has now emerged that Hankook is ready to throw its hat into the ring too and has been secretly ramping up its own efforts.
Representatives of the company were spotted at the recent Las Vegas Grand Prix, which was understood to have been their second visit to an F1 race this year following a trip to Madrid in September.
The Race understands that Hankook has used these trips to meet a majority of teams and discuss plans with bosses, CEOs and other senior executives.
The trips to races, which also included visits to events in China, Japan and Singapore in 2025, are only one side of its efforts to get ready for 2029, however.
It is understood that Hankook has already committed a 44-person task force within the company to prepare for an F1 entry.

Beyond committing research and development capability plus simulator running, it has this year completed two development tests for F1 rubber using a modified F2-equivalent-mule car to evaluate potential construction as well as different compounds.

A third test has been scheduled to work on its wet-weather rubber, which it hopes can also help it develop a tyre that features a narrower spray plume to reduce visibility problems caused in wet conditions.
Hankook is also working hard on production and manufacturing planning that would be required to supply F1, F2 and F3 tyres that would come under the umbrella of any tyre tender contract.

Hankook is certainly no stranger to FIA competition, with the South Korean company already the official tyre supplier to the World Rally Championship and has just ended its supply to Formula E where Bridgestone is taking over for the upcoming season. Earlier this year Hankook was also named as a global partner of the governing body.

The period of the new F1 tyre tender beyond 2029 will almost certainly cover the transition to the next rules era, with F1 setting sights on new lighter and nimbler cars to coincide with the switch to V8 power units from 2030.
The plans are also set to include a new tyre design, which is set to reduce wheel size slightly from the current 18-inch design.
